transcript: Last night I attended love at Park Avenue Armory, which I had never been to, and I was so shocked by how gorgeous and massive it is. Love is a small, intimate portrait of 8 people living in a temporary housing facility in England. At the theater, we often see really big, dramatic events that make people erupt into song, for example, and that's what engages us in this piece. Drama comes from things like a dispute over the ownership of a mug or the anxieties around sharing a bathroom with other people. In the context of this richly subtle play, seemingly tiny interactions can carry huge emotional weight, as the characters are in such precarious circumstances. I really, really enjoyed this piece, and although it's quite relevant to New York City, where currently around 70,000 people are experiencing homelessness, I couldn't help but notice the irony that this is being produced in one of the wealthiest neighborhoods in Manhattan. With that, another program for my collection.
